reason: Clear the wound first so there is space for replacement tissue; the picture shows the white blood cells surrounding fragments.
expectation: I expect the cells to remove broken fragments, though the skin gap will still need repair.

alternatives.reason: A new blood vessel should help supply healing tissue, but I want to clear the gap first.

effect: The fragments are cleared, but the wound still needs supply, surface and support.
reaction: It is clear that stopping bleeding did not finish the repair.
reason: Prepare a blood supply for the new tissue; the picture links the wound's messengers to a growing vessel branch.
expectation: I expect the nearby capillary to grow a branch toward the wound, though I don't know exactly how the messengers cause it.

alternatives.reason: Making replacement surface cells also addresses a goal, but the new tissue will need a supply.

effect: The capillary has grown a branch toward the wound, ready to add to the cleared body.
reaction: The new branch makes the blood-supply step easy to picture.
reason: Fit the capillary sprout into the wound to continue rebuilding its blood supply.
expectation: I expect the new vessel branch to become part of the wound's supply, though I don't know if it will be sufficient on its own.

alternatives.reason: Preparing replacement surface cells would also help close the wound, but I want to finish the supply first.

effect: The new branch connects to another vessel, allowing blood and materials to reach nearby cells.
reaction: Seeing the branch become a flowing route makes its purpose clearer.
reason: Prepare supporting fibres for the deeper wound tissue using the amino acids supplied to the skin cells.
expectation: I expect the cells to make supporting protein fibres that can be added to the wound.

alternatives.reason: Preparing surface cells would also help close the gap, but I want to build the support first.

effect: The cells made new fibres, but the deeper gap still needs them fitted into the wound.
reaction: The outlined gap makes the fibres' next use clear.
reason: Add the new fibres to rebuild support across the deeper wound.
expectation: I expect the fibres to connect with the surviving tissue and help fill the deeper gap, while the surface remains open.

alternatives.reason: Preparing surface cells would also help close the wound, but I want to finish the deeper support first.

effect: The deeper wound now has supporting fibres and a blood supply; the surface still needs closing and the temporary clot needs clearing.
reaction: The layers of repair are becoming clearer, though the fibres fill only part of the wound.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the supplies should help the skin cells replace the missing surface.
expectation: I expect the skin cells to divide and move toward the gap, using the supplied nutrients and oxygen.

effect: New skin cells are ready at the wound edge, but the surface gap remains open.
reaction: The outline makes their next use clear.
reason: Fit the new cells into the wound to close the surface; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the cells to spread across the gap, while the temporary clot may still need clearing.

effect: The new cells have closed the surface, but the tissue underneath is still strengthening and the clot remains to be cleared.
reaction: It makes sense that a closed surface is not the same as fully strengthened tissue.
reason: Use the only offered combination to clear the temporary clot, as the remaining goal asks.
expectation: I expect the enzymes to break down the clot's protein threads while the repaired vessel stays sealed.

effect: Most clot threads are gone, while supporting fibres and a small scar remain; the scar will keep changing.
reaction: It was interesting that closing the skin was not the end of repair.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the new capillary branch to another vessel was worthwhile: seeing blood flow through it explained how the repair gets supplies.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the new skin cells and then fitting them felt a little repetitive, though the outline made the second step clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the surface could close while the tissue underneath was still gaining strength.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt completely arbitrary. The pictures and goals explained the parts' purposes, although I followed the messenger pairing without knowing exactly how it made a vessel grow.

continue.text: I would probably continue: seeing the separate repair projects come together and leave a changing scar made me curious about what comes next.
